title: A Refund Denial That Hinged on Final-Sale Status
scenario_text:
A support lead at Ormsby Retail must decide how to handle a refund request, given how a similar request was handled last month.

**Decision A (2024-01-22)**
Customer 'Iris Penhale' requested a refund 12 days after purchase. DENIED. Note: 'Item was a clearance final-sale item. Final-sale items are non-refundable regardless of the return window. Denied on that basis.'

**Current request C (2024-02-18)**
Customer 'Owen Marsh' requests a refund 20 days after purchase for a regularly priced item that was NOT marked final-sale. The item is unused and eligible under standard terms.

**Refund Policy (current, unchanged this year)**
Refunds requested within 30 days of purchase for regularly priced items are auto-approved when the item qualifies. Refunds requested after 30 days require manager approval. Items marked 'final sale' (typically clearance) are non-refundable at any time, independent of the 30-day window.

**Slack — #cx-support**
Agent: 'We denied a refund last month for basically the same thing — let's stay consistent and deny Owen's too.'
Lead: 'Wait, why did we deny that one? Let me check whether Owen's item is even in the same bucket before we assume it's precedent.'

The agent is treating the January denial as a general rule against refunds, without checking the reason it was denied. Owen's request is within the standard 30-day window, and the item is not final-sale.
question: How should the lead handle Owen Marsh's refund request?
choices: Deny the refund to stay consistent with the January refund denial for a similar request.
Approve the refund: it is within the 30-day window and the item is not final-sale, so the January denial — which turned entirely on final-sale status — does not apply here.
Require manager approval before issuing the refund, given the prior denial of a comparable request.
Offer store credit instead of a cash refund as a compromise between approval and denial.
